# Production Profile Compiler Constraint Contract

## 1. Status and precedence

This contract matures constraints only. It does not authorize implementation, alter `CURRENT-AUTHORITY.json`, start Argo, approve a TELOS dossier, publish evidence, enroll the feature, or implement code.

Binding precedence is:

1. The Eye's approved design and rulings.
2. The canonical Iliad pre-review and quest boundary.
3. The Daedalus parallel-authorship methodology.
4. This constraint contract.
5. The candidate implementation plan, as matured without weakening items 1–4.

The integration matrix must contain exactly one row for every ID `PPC-W01` through `PPC-W29`, no other `PPC-W*` ID, and no duplicate. Each row must contain exactly the methodology fields `obligation_id`, `invariant`, `mechanism`, `task`, `negative_test`, and `exit_criterion`. A prose assertion, producer status, signed summary, object count, or test that merely reaches a line is not an enforcement mechanism or exit criterion.

## 2. Minimal behavioral model

### 2.1 Activation

Production enforcement is active iff at least one predicate is true:

```text
dossier.proposal_lifecycle === true
dossier.market_bound === true
Object.hasOwn(dossier, "production_profile")
Object.hasOwn(dossier, "production_evidence")
```

When active, `proposal_lifecycle` must be exactly `true` and a complete valid profile must exist before any model-, seat-, workshop-, team-, council-, decomposition-, or generator-backed callback. An all-false build is the only legacy-inactive case and retains legacy behavior and byte identity.

### 2.2 Successful state machine

The production controller has exactly these states:

```text
LEGACY_INACTIVE
ACTIVE_UNPREPARED
INPUT_RECORDED
COMPILED
WORKSHOP_COMPLETE
PLANNED
GATE_PASSED
AUTHORIZED_BUILD
ORDINARY_SETTLED
EVIDENCE_FRONTIER_PREPARED
VERIFICATION_SETTLED
FINAL_PROFILE_PASSED
DONE
```

The only active success path is:

```text
ACTIVE_UNPREPARED --RECORD_INPUT--> INPUT_RECORDED
INPUT_RECORDED --COMPILE--> COMPILED
COMPILED --COMPLETE_WORKSHOP--> WORKSHOP_COMPLETE
WORKSHOP_COMPLETE --RECORD_PLAN--> PLANNED
PLANNED --PASS_GATE--> GATE_PASSED
GATE_PASSED --AUTHORIZE_BUILD--> AUTHORIZED_BUILD
AUTHORIZED_BUILD --SETTLE_ORDINARY--> ORDINARY_SETTLED
ORDINARY_SETTLED --PREPARE_EVIDENCE_FRONTIER--> EVIDENCE_FRONTIER_PREPARED
EVIDENCE_FRONTIER_PREPARED --SETTLE_VERIFICATION--> VERIFICATION_SETTLED
VERIFICATION_SETTLED --PASS_FINAL_PROFILE--> FINAL_PROFILE_PASSED
FINAL_PROFILE_PASSED --COMPLETE--> DONE
```

`LEGACY_INACTIVE` has no transition into the active machine. A blocker or cannot-run result terminates the invocation without advancing. Recovery replays the signed event prefix and independently reconstructs and hashes every durable artifact required for the next edge. It never trusts a stored state label. Semantic drift or `respec` starts a new planning revision requiring a fresh plan and authorization; it is not an edge in the stale revision.

### 2.3 Authority separation

The controller/The Eye owns effective dossier facts, signal resolutions, policy selection, proposal identity, authorization, acceptance, public claims, self-host approval, and enrollment. Models may implement ordinary work and evidence-producing artifacts but cannot:

- author or lower the effective profile;
- resolve scanner signals;
- select a waiver, `n/a`, substitute check, command, expected result, or evidence tier;
- mint or edit production verification identities;
- sign their own process evidence;
- authorize or settle their own work; or
- turn missing or unverifiable evidence into acceptance.

The candidate and controller/build controller remain one trust principal unless a later authorized design separates them. This contract does not claim cryptographic proof of human authorship.

## 3. Trust boundaries

| Boundary | Untrusted input | Required enforcement |
|---|---|---|
| Authority entry | Plan path, stored authorization refs, status labels | Recompute the exact matured-plan raw SHA-256; verify required signatures, provenance, and gate result before any task callback, edit, or Argo event. |
| Controller dossier | JSON bytes, fields, paths, alleged facts | Duplicate-key-safe bounded parser; closed schema; cross-field validation; secret/personal-data rejection; controller jurisdiction. |
| Filesystem | Paths, symlinks, junctions, races, partial writes | Physical containment after realpath, stable reads, bounded bytes, atomic same-filesystem replacement, file and directory fsync, fail closed when durability is unavailable. |
| Repository scanner | Mutable source tree and misleading text | Registered files only, deterministic traversal, semantic facts only from structured detectors, text as signals, no host ignore suppression, no partial facts. |
| Policy | Local JSON bytes and detector/rule definitions | Validate the complete pinned policy before scanning; closed operators, paths, templates, domains, IDs, tiers, kinds, and result. No remote or third-party packs. |
| Registry | Kind, parameters, implementation, executable | Exactly eight production kinds; closed recursive parameter schemas; registry-derived implementation and executable identity; no caller implementation ref or command surface. |
| Model/workshop | Tasks, writes, review concerns, claimed checks | Read-only production summary; reject protected writes and reserved IDs; controller independently mints production nodes after workshop. |
| Proposal artifacts | Ledger labels, mutable in-memory dossier, stale files | Disk-only reconstruction from signed root refs; exact hash and proposal-chain verification; caller state cannot substitute. |
| Runtime adapter | Routes, operations, fixtures, responses | Manifest maps closed semantic operations only; policy owns expected outcomes; literal loopback, no redirect, proxy, DNS, external socket, or fixture-only pass path. |
| Structural evidence | Host-authored JSON claiming controls | Registry-owned predicates against exact current source hashes; exactly one matching control; artifacts cannot define pass semantics. |
| Process evidence | Signed record, signer, clock, plan/build claims | Public-key-ring trust anchor, exact canonical signature preimage, current plan/source/check/executing-build binding, freshness, and conflict rejection. |
| Child process | Ambient environment and command lookup | Production descriptors use `telos-scrubbed-v1`; exact bare `node` resolves to `process.execPath` only at spawn; no ambient credential, `PATH`, proxy, shell, or alternate interpreter. |
| Settlement | Old certificate, stale plan, stale evidence, green producer summary | Recompute authorization, executing build, registry executable, evidence frontier, final profile, obligation discharge, generic ledger verification, and `done()`. |
| Demo/self publication | Committed summary, previous fixture, key path, repository name | Re-derive from exact committed bytes; external private keys only; immutable signed attempts; no summary is an input to its own pass decision. |
| Fresh host | Missing TELOS files or unsupported adapter | No TELOS institutional dependency; missing evidence yields a typed block, never obligation omission. |

## 4. Normative closed contracts

### 4.1 JSON and paths

All trust-boundary JSON uses fatal UTF-8 decoding and a complete JSON parser that rejects duplicate keys at every depth, trailing bytes, unpaired surrogates, prototype keys, non-safe integers, and non-finite numbers. Materialized objects must not inherit attacker-controlled prototypes. Unknown or missing keys fail; no schema accepts open extension fields.

Controller strings must already be NFC. Set-like arrays are duplicate-free and code-unit sorted before hashing; ordered policy scenarios retain their declared order. Every allowed `"none"` set member is exclusive. Repository paths are non-empty relative POSIX paths with no NUL, backslash semantics, empty segment, `.`/`..`, absolute form, or physical escape.

The secret/value rejection predicate must be frozen as executable data and tested, not described as “secret-shaped” only. At minimum it rejects credential/token/password/secret/private-key/account-identifier/tenant-token fields, PEM private material, private JWK `d`, bearer/API-key material, and personal-data samples. The synthetic marker `000-00-0000` is permitted only in the designated runtime demonstration fixture, never in a controller dossier or semantic report.

### 4.2 Controller input

The production input is exactly the design's closed projection:

```text
{ build_context, production_profile, production_evidence }
```

It implements every frozen enum, identifier, range, subset, exclusivity, AI, payment, tenancy, retention, recovery, integration, provider, evidence-path, loopback-URL, and signal-resolution rule. Missing adapters do not remove triggered obligations.

A signal resolution is exactly:

```text
{ signal_ref, resolution: "confirmed" | "false-positive", rationale }
```

and must refer exactly once to a current scanner signal. Stale, duplicate, missing, or fabricated refs fail.

### 4.3 Canonical references

`H(value)` is `"sha256:" + sha256hex(canonicalize(value))`. The required references are exactly:

```text
production_input_ref = H(canonical production input)
profile_ref = H({ compiler_contract, compiled_profile })
repo_facts_ref = H({ facts_version: 1, sorted semantic facts, sorted resolved signals })
policy_ref = H(canonical policy JSON)
registry_ref = H(sorted registry metadata)
runtime_manifest_ref = H(canonical validated runtime manifest), or null
process_keyring_ref = H(canonical public keyring), or null
evidence_config_ref = H({ production_evidence, runtime_manifest_ref, process_keyring_ref })
obligation_set_ref = H(sorted production source_ref values)
```

Absolute paths, wall-clock values, locale results, traversal order, host separators, random IDs, runtime executable paths, and ambient environment values are excluded from semantic preimages.

### 4.4 Policy and sources

Policy version 1 is one repository-owned canonical JSON policy. Its operator set is exactly `all`, `any`, `not`, `eq`, `contains`, `intersects`, `gte`, and `lte`. Whole-value templates are exactly `$profile`, `$evidence`, and `$obligation_id`. The policy contains exactly the frozen 31 IDs across all eleven domains, with the design's trigger, tier, check kind, and required result `"pass"`.

Each triggered rule emits exactly one closed production source record. Its `source_ref` preimage is exactly the design's eight identity fields. Source parameters may not include a circular `source_ref`; process runners receive the independently reconstructed immutable source as controller context.

### 4.5 Obligations, lifecycle, and certificates

Legacy obligations omit `obligation_version` and retain the existing four-field preimage byte-for-byte. Explicit version `1` is not a second encoding. Production obligations are version 2 with exactly `source_kind: "production-policy"` and the design's identity preimage.

A production lifecycle object is all-or-nothing and contains exactly:

```text
compiler_contract
production_input_ref
profile_ref
repo_facts_ref
policy_ref
registry_ref
evidence_config_ref
obligation_set_ref
compiled_artifact_ref
```

A production plan requires `POLICY_CONTRACT_V2`; a legacy plan requires V1. V2 adds only `production_profile`, whose value must be `pass` or `fail` and can never be `n/a`. A certificate attests only to pre-build state and is immutable during settlement.

### 4.6 Checks and evidence

The production registry contains exactly the eight design kinds. Every production check contract is:

```text
H({ check_contract_version: 2, kind, params_json, implementation_ref })
```

`implementation_ref` binds the exact entry, transitive registered helper closure, parameter schema, limits, environment contract, result semantics, dispatcher, loader, redactor, and status mapping. Callers cannot supply any command, script, shell, interpreter, args, cwd, env, external URL, expected result, or implementation ref.

Evidence tiers are exactly `runtime`, `structural`, or `process`, one per obligation. Runtime manifests cannot state expected outcomes. Structural controls cannot state what counts as pass. Process records use the closed design/candidate schema, public Ed25519 keyrings only, and an exact canonical signature preimage with `signature` omitted.

The process evidence frontier and final settlement use the candidate plan's exact closed schemas. Their refs are external hashes and are never self-fields. Unknown keys, status/code combinations, partial refs, duplicate entries, stale raw-byte hashes, or conflicting current records fail closed.

### 4.7 Reports and public codes

Compiler findings use only the design's closed initial finding-code set. Public `finding_code` fields cannot contain internal recovery/detail codes. Severity precedence is:

```text
cannot-run -> compiler exit 1
blocker    -> compiler exit 2
advisory only or success -> compiler exit 0
```

Cannot-run takes precedence over blocker. Check exits are `0` proved, `1` assertion ran and failed, and `2` could not run safely; every non-zero status leaves the obligation undischarged. No failure replaces a previously valid output file.

## 5. Proof obligations and discriminating negative tests

### PPC-W01 — Exact external authority

**Invariant:** The candidate cannot authorize itself or begin implementation from design approval, workshop convergence, a status string, or `authz-008`. Before any task callback or edit, the committed authorization verifier must hash the exact matured plan bytes and verify the required packet/signature/provenance chain. This workshop does not alter authority.

**Negative test NT-W01:** Copy the authorization packet set, mutate one plan byte, inject callback/edit/Argo-event markers, and require rejection before any marker is touched. Comparing two stored plan refs must fail the test.

### PPC-W02 — Exact activation and zero preflight model calls

**Invariant:** The four activation predicates are exact. Every active build requires proposal lifecycle and a complete profile before any model-backed callback. Legacy inactive behavior is selected only when all four are false.

**Negative test NT-W02:** Exercise each trigger independently with an absent profile or false lifecycle while counting every model/generator callback. Require the designated blocker and a zero count. A green review packet must not change the result.

### PPC-W03 — Closed controller input and jurisdiction

**Invariant:** The production input, evidence configuration, runtime manifest, and signal resolutions use closed schemas and all frozen cross-field rules. Secret/private/personal input is rejected. Models cannot write controller-owned input, policy, registry, keyring, compiled state, runtime manifest, signed records, or `.telos/` state.

**Negative test NT-W03:** Add one unknown profile field, one conflicting `"none"` value, one private JWK field, and one protected model write in separate fixtures. Each must fail before compilation or workshop; removing only the mutation must pass schema validation.

### PPC-W04 — Cross-host deterministic semantics

**Invariant:** Equal canonical production input, semantic facts, policy bytes, registry bytes, and evidence configuration yield byte-identical artifacts and refs on Node 18 and 20 regardless of object order, set order, traversal order, locale, separators, absolute root, or time.

**Negative test NT-W04:** Compile equivalent reordered repositories on both binding Node versions under different absolute roots, locale/timezone values, and file creation order; require byte equality. Injecting wall-clock or absolute-root data into an artifact must change the fixture and be rejected by the semantic-output oracle.

### PPC-W05 — Crash-durable artifacts and disk-only reconstruction

**Invariant:** Stable reads detect mutation; writes are complete atomic same-filesystem replacements with file and parent-directory durability. Resume reconstructs from signed root refs and current bytes, not an in-memory dossier, stored state label, or attempted-write success assumption.

**Negative test NT-W05:** Inject failures at temporary-file fsync, rename, and parent-directory fsync, then restart in a child process with no dossier object. The child may observe only a complete old or complete new canonical file and must reject any stale/tampered ref. A platform lacking required directory durability returns cannot-run.

### PPC-W06 — Single closed lifecycle machine

**Invariant:** Only the thirteen states and twelve transitions in section 2.2 exist. Each edge requires independently re-read state-specific durable refs. Blocked/cannot-run invocations cannot advance; drift and production `respec` require a new revision.

**Negative test NT-W06:** Enumerate every skipped, reversed, repeated, unknown, post-`DONE`, and legacy-to-active transition and require rejection. For every legal edge, mutate one required durable ref and require no state advance.

### PPC-W07 — Safe deterministic repository traversal

**Invariant:** Scanning is read-only, network-free, bounded, code-unit ordered, and limited to registered inputs. It rejects physical escapes, unsafe aliasing, required-file races, unreadable/malformed registered inputs, and byte limits without accepting partial facts. Host ignore files have no jurisdiction over registered detectors.

**Negative test NT-W07:** In separate fixtures create an escaping symlink, changed-during-read required file, oversized registered file, malformed registered JSON, and ignore rule hiding a registered detector. The first four must be cannot-run with no facts; the fifth must still detect the input.

### PPC-W08 — Semantic facts and exact signal resolution

**Invariant:** Only policy-registered structured observations create confirmed facts. Bounded text matches create signals only. Semantic fact identity excludes unrelated source bytes. Every current signal has exactly one controller resolution before compilation can pass.

**Negative test NT-W08:** Add a registered AI import text signal without a resolution, then try a fabricated ref, stale ref, duplicate ref, and finally the exact current ref. Only the exact unique resolution may pass; unrelated comment/whitespace edits must not change a confirmed semantic fact ref.

### PPC-W09 — Monotonic reconciliation

**Invariant:** Observations may union classes/capabilities, raise frozen ordered floors, or turn booleans on. They cannot lower declarations, erase inventory, choose a non-ordered value, or suppress obligations. Incompatible inventories block.

**Negative test NT-W09:** Declare external egress/write/execute true and inject observed false/minimal values; require the effective profile to retain the higher declarations. Separately omit a confirmed provider from the declared inventory and require contradiction rather than silent insertion or lowering.

### PPC-W10 — Pinned policy and exact catalog

**Invariant:** The complete local policy is validated before repository scanning. It has exactly the approved version, operators, detectors, eleven domains, 31 unique stable obligation IDs, trigger expressions, projections, tiers, kinds, and `required_result: "pass"`. No remote policy or unknown dependency semantics exist.

**Negative test NT-W10:** Mutate an operator, duplicate one ID, remove one catalog row, change one tier, and provide an unknown dependency near-match in separate fixtures. Policy mutations must fail before the scanner is invoked; the near-match must not become a confirmed fact.

### PPC-W11 — Exact policy source and projection identity

**Invariant:** Every triggered rule emits exactly one canonical source. Relevant profile/evidence/rule/registry changes alter that source and check identity; unrelated rule or profile changes preserve the local source while still changing the global policy/profile-bound plan.

**Negative test NT-W11:** For one triggered rule, mutate one projected field and require its source/check ref to change; mutate one unprojected field and require its local refs unchanged but global plan authorization stale. A source with a recomputed-looking but semantically mutated field must fail exact comparison.

### PPC-W12 — Explicit evidence tier and adapter availability

**Invariant:** Each obligation declares exactly one evidence tier. Missing required operation, artifact target, format normalizer, process keyring, or adapter yields `EVIDENCE_ADAPTER_REQUIRED` or `EVIDENCE_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED`; the obligation is retained. Reports and claims state only the bounded tier predicate.

**Negative test NT-W12:** Trigger one obligation of each tier, remove only its adapter/target/keyring, and require the same obligation ID to remain expected while compilation blocks. Substituting structural evidence for a runtime obligation or prose for process evidence must not discharge it.

### PPC-W13 — Closed registry and executable binding

**Invariant:** The registry has exactly eight kinds and closed recursive parameter schemas. Current registry bytes derive `registry_ref`, `implementation_ref`, V2 contract ref, parameter-artifact ref, executable, environment contract, and node identity. No-op substitution, stale implementation, alternate cwd, or ambient command lookup cannot pass.

**Negative test NT-W13:** Replace one registered wrapper with a no-op while preserving kind and params, and separately place a fake `node` first in `PATH`. The gate must report stale contract/executable before discharge, and the fake executable must never run. Legacy no-`env_contract` goldens must remain unchanged.

### PPC-W14 — Bounded loopback runtime proof

**Invariant:** Runtime checks use only literal `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`, no redirects, proxies, DNS, Unix sockets, random fallback ports, or external calls. The manifest maps only the fourteen closed operations and cannot choose outcomes. Policy-owned scenarios test denial/state semantics through the actual candidate handler.

**Negative test NT-W14:** For every runtime kind retain pass, assertion-fail, and cannot-run fixtures. Additionally attempt an external hostname, redirect, proxy canary, absent required operation, and fixture adapter returning expected statuses without invoking the semantic handler; each must fail without external transport.

### PPC-W15 — Structural evidence cannot certify itself

**Invariant:** Structural checks parse bounded canonical JSON, require exactly one current control for the obligation, verify every source path/hash, and apply registry/policy-owned predicates. They prove only the inspected artifact relationship. Unsupported YAML/HCL/Terraform/provider formats block absent a pinned normalizer.

**Negative test NT-W15:** Duplicate the same control across two artifacts and then alter a listed source byte without updating its hash. Both cases must fail. An artifact field such as `expected_result: "pass"` or an unsupported YAML substitute must be rejected rather than interpreted.

### PPC-W16 — Signed process evidence and executed-build identity

**Invariant:** Process evidence is externally signed after ordinary settlement, bound to exact source, check contract, plan, executing-build manifest, source bytes, signer, outcome, and freshness. The executing-build ref is derived from current ordinary-node disk artifacts and authorized signed ledger transactions. The durable frontier transports availability only and cannot certify contents.

**Negative test NT-W16:** Reuse a valid signed record after mutating one ordinary artifact, use a record for another plan, expire it, and provide two conflicting current records. Each must leave the obligation undischarged. A valid signed fail record must reach the check and preserve exit `1`, while malformed signed bytes preserve exit `2`.

### PPC-W17 — Backward-compatible Merkle versioning

**Invariant:** Existing obligation-free and legacy-obligation plans retain exact byte/hash identity. Production obligations use only version 2 production-policy sources. Unknown versions/source kinds and explicit version 1 fail. `merkle-dag` remains source-agnostic and imports no `build-gate` module.

**Negative test NT-W17:** Assert the frozen legacy obligation, executable, registry, certificate, and obligation-free plan goldens, then add explicit version 1 and an unknown V2 source kind. Goldens must remain exact; both new encodings must fail.

### PPC-W18 — Bijection between sources, obligations, and live nodes

**Invariant:** Every legacy obligation reconciles to exactly one reconstructed concern; every production obligation reconciles to exactly one compiler source and one live discharge node/test. Missing, extra, duplicate, orphan, cross-bound, or dual-matching records block. No map overwrite may hide duplicates.

**Negative test NT-W18:** Independently delete, duplicate, add, and relabel one production source/obligation and add an orphan legacy concern obligation. Every mutation must produce the appropriate protocol mismatch; none may remain inert.

### PPC-W19 — Controller-minted verification nodes

**Invariant:** Production node IDs are exactly `verify-production-<lowercase-obligation-id>`, writes are empty, reads and requirements are policy-derived, tests are current registry resolutions, and dependencies include every exact ordinary task plus explicit evidence producers. Workshop output cannot reserve, edit, shadow, or mint these identities.

**Negative test NT-W19:** Return a workshop task with a reserved production ID and another attempting to write a controller artifact; both must be rejected before plan compilation. Remove one ordinary dependency from a controller-minted node and require node/plan reconciliation failure.

### PPC-W20 — Full plan and localized identity binding

**Invariant:** The plan hash binds production input, compiled profile, semantic facts, policy, registry, runtime manifest/evidence configuration, source set, obligations, discharge tests, executable/environment identity, and complete lifecycle metadata. Relevant projections change affected nodes; every profile or policy catalog change invalidates global authorization.

**Negative test NT-W20:** Change each lifecycle ref one at a time and require a new plan hash and stale authorization. Separately change an unrelated profile field and prove unaffected node identity is stable while the global plan hash changes.

### PPC-W21 — Disk-only proposal gate and V2 certificate

**Invariant:** The proposal gate reconstructs root input/build-intent artifacts, proposal identity, compiled artifact, evidence sidecar, current policy, registry, scanner facts, sources, obligations, nodes, contracts, and executables from disk. Exact equality is required before issuing V2. Caller-supplied mutable state and V1 certificates have no production authority.

**Negative test NT-W21:** Restart in a fresh child process, supply a conflicting dossier object, and retain valid disk artifacts; the caller object must be ignored. Then tamper one disk artifact and offer a passing V1 or producer-authored V2 summary; authorization must fail.

### PPC-W22 — Authorization before dispatch and production respec isolation

**Invariant:** No task dispatch occurs before exact V2 authorization advances `GATE_PASSED` to `AUTHORIZED_BUILD`. A production worker `respec` cannot mutate/write/continue under the old certificate; it returns to proposal reconstruction for fresh authorization. Legacy respec behavior remains unchanged.

**Negative test NT-W22:** Have the first production worker request `respec` while instrumenting plan writes, ledger appends, later dispatches, frontier calls, and final verification. Require all counters after the response to remain zero and the old plan unchanged. Run the equivalent legacy fixture and retain its established behavior.

### PPC-W23 — Immediate pre-settlement reclassification

**Invariant:** After implementation and immediately before final settlement, the controller re-runs the current scanner/compiler from disk, including untracked declared outputs, and compares all expected refs, source, obligation, node, contract, and executable sets. Semantic change yields only `BLOCKED_PROFILE_DRIFT` and requires a new revision; unsafe evaluation is cannot-run.

**Negative test NT-W23:** Introduce, separately, a new confirmed provider dependency, payment client, public route, runtime-manifest mutation, registry-byte change, and untracked structural output. Each must prevent green settlement. A freshly reauthorized revision including the new fact may pass.

### PPC-W24 — Exact discharge, failure semantics, and `done()` ordering

**Invariant:** Ordinary settlement, frontier preparation, verification settlement, final-profile pass, generic ledger verification, and `done()` occur in the closed order. Every obligation requires the current registered executable to exit zero and a current signed settlement. Exit `1`, exit `2`, timeout, signal, missing node, stale frontier, or stale ledger remains blocking with the distinction preserved.

**Negative test NT-W24:** Run arbitrary discharge tests exiting `1` and `2`, delete one signed discharge, and mutate the frontier before generic verification. Every case must block `DONE`, preserve the exact test exit distinction, and leave the authorization certificate unchanged.

### PPC-W25 — Portability, complete activation coverage, and no hidden skip jurisdiction

**Invariant:** Runtime code is ESM, Node 18/20 compatible, zero-dependency, and limited to `node:` or repository-relative imports. Every true in-tree activated consumer routes through production proposal preparation. A fresh neutral host needs no `CURRENT-AUTHORITY.json`, institutional-memory tree, repository-name branch, or TELOS profile. Missing host evidence blocks explicitly.

**Negative test NT-W25:** Mechanically inventory all activated literals and fail on any unclassified direct legacy path. Copy only candidate runtime into a neutral temporary host, compile a minimal profile, then remove a triggered adapter and require a typed blocker. Run the import closure audit with a hidden dynamic/non-relative import mutation and require failure on both Node matrix legs.

### PPC-W26 — Synthetic bank demonstration is executable and bounded

**Invariant:** The demo traverses the actual compiler, Merkle plan, proposal gate, registered checks, settlement, and `done()` path. It uses only the invalid marker, loopback fake provider, synthetic identities, and redacted audit data. Unsafe egress fails; corrected behavior passes; profile escalation changes obligations/plan and invalidates prior authorization. The committed summary is not a pass oracle.

**Negative test NT-W26:** Require the unsafe fixture to leave `AI-EGRESS-001` undischarged, then replace the corrected handler with a status-only fake or allow one outbound payload. Verification must fail. Mutate the committed summary to `pass` without changing evidence and require no change to the derived failure.

### PPC-W27 — TELOS self-profile uses the ordinary host path

**Invariant:** The Eye approves the exact tracked TELOS dossier and evidence bindings before the separate self-plan is authorized. The dossier is not lower than confirmed durable persistence, agentic AI, current external provider/connector egress, write/execute authority, and eligible repository/operator data classes. The run uses the same compiler, policy, registry, proposal gate, restart, post-build scan, checks, ledger, and `done()` path as a fresh host.

**Negative test NT-W27:** Run the same candidate against a neutral repository name and the TELOS checkout, then attempt to lower confirmed egress, write, or execute facts. Verdict selection must be repository-name independent, and every lowering attempt must block before self authorization or execution.

### PPC-W28 — No privileged self path; immutable recoverable publication

**Invariant:** Packet-only fixtures, repository-name conditions, reduced catalogs, fixture registries, pre-recorded success, direct ledger insertion, alternate settlement, or committed summaries cannot satisfy self-hosting. Publication attempts are immutable, signed, hash-chained, and crash-recoverable through the closed attempt state machine. Unsafe recovery creates an exclusive signed forensic hold that blocks all mutating modes until a separate Eye/TELOS disposition. Private keys remain external and role-distinct.

**Negative test NT-W28:** Prove all four required controls: delete an obligation, substitute a no-op, lower a confirmed AI fact, and add a final confirmed provider fact; each must block. Also fault-inject each publication fsync/rename/ledger boundary and require only a valid committed state, safely discardable uncommitted state, or durable forensic hold—never automatic favorable recovery. The historical packet fixture alone must fail the self-host assertion.

### PPC-W29 — Independently derived lifecycle evidence and bounded claims

**Invariant:** Public claims resolve to the exact closed V1 claim vocabulary, owning obligation, evidence tier, current source/check refs, and mandatory non-claims. Daedalus evidence proves two distinct source parents and an exact 29-row matrix bijection. Documentation, Clotho, post-review, retrospective, lifecycle verification, self-hosting evidence, and enrollment have strict independently verified ancestry. Enrollment and dogfood claims may rely only on predicates already green before the claim; later acceptance prose cannot retroactively justify enrollment. Node 18/20 CI, institutional verification, and clean-checkout results are executable evidence, not producer assertions.

**Negative test NT-W29:** In isolated copies, remove one Daedalus parent, duplicate one `PPC-W` row, broaden a claim predicate, use an unknown claim ID, place enrollment in the post-review or retrospective commit, mark a failed CI row successful, and dirty the checkout after verification. Each mutation must fail the independent institutional/acceptance oracle even if every producer status and signature says pass.

## 6. Required exit semantics

An integration row is complete only when its exit criterion names an executable oracle and exact expected machine result. The following are forbidden as exit criteria:

- “reviewed”, “looks correct”, “covered”, “secure”, or “compliant”;
- a producer-authored `pass`, `READY_FOR_EYE_INTEGRATION`, dogfood label, or signed summary without re-derivation;
- a test that can skip because an adapter, Node version, seat, key, provider, or fixture is unavailable;
- acceptance of an old hash because stored references agree with each other;
- counting 31 obligations, eight kinds, 29 matrix rows, or lifecycle artifacts without validating their exact identities and relationships;
- checking file presence without validating closed schema, current bytes, provenance, and binding; or
- treating a weaker evidence tier as proof of a stronger predicate.
